name: Money-Mouth Face
baseMeaning: A face with dollar sign eyes and a bill coming out of its mouth.
tldr: 🤑 closes money jokes about payday, income, greed, or an absurd price, depending on the sentence.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🝒 shows a face with dollar-sign eyes and a banknote protruding from its mouth.
contextMeanings.example: look at this face, dollar signs in its eyes and cash in its mouth 🤑

contextMeanings.meaning: 🤑 expresses anticipation or excitement about money that is about to arrive.
🤑 turns a boast about someone’s own income into a knowingly smug joke.
contextMeanings.example: me finally explaining this side hustle 🤑

contextMeanings.meaning: Under a price, 🤑 can imply that the amount is excessive without clarifying who cannot afford it.

platformNotes.note: On iMessage, 🤑 works naturally as the final mark after a casual money update. The visible sentence usually clarifies whether it means anticipation, a boast, or disbelief about a price.

In an Instagram caption, 🤑 can punctuate a payoff, a payday joke, or a story about receiving payment. In comments, it often reacts to someone else’s income or price rather than telling a complete story.
In TikTok captions and comments, 🤑 can play as an exaggerated flex about earning money. The joke may be sincere or deliberately ironic, so nearby words still carry much of the meaning.
In Slack, a bare 🤑 in a work channel can sound smug or overly playful about compensation. A specific message about a payment date or reimbursement is safer than relying on the face alone.

generationalNotes.note: For Gen Z, 🤑 can work as a knowingly exaggerated flex about money arriving or income growing. The dramatic face often fits the joke better than a calm businesslike message.
Millennials may read 🤑 as a mixture of payday excitement and showing off. Older, more restrained wording can make the same emoji sound more boastful than intended.
Boomers may hear the dollar signs and protruding cash more literally, making 🤑 seem plainly greedy. Clear wording about receiving, spending, or requesting money helps prevent that reading.

warnings.title: Greed or broke?
warnings.description: Under a price, 🤑 may mean “that costs too much for me” or “you are charging too much.” State the amount plainly, and use 💸 when you mean money has already been spent.

warnings.title: The flex can sound like an insult
warnings.description: A boast about the sender’s income can also read as a jab at someone else’s finances. Keep the joke clearly focused on yourself, or replace it with a plain payment update.

seoDescription: What does 🤑 mean? It shows excitement about incoming money, an ironic boast about income, or a joking objection to a price, depending on the sentence.

longForm.overview:
🤑 is the emoji you put at the end when money is the punchline. Dollar-sign eyes and a banknote poking from its mouth make the face look greedy, but the text usually decides what kind of greed: excitement about money arriving, a boast about income, or an objection to a price. It commonly closes a line such as “invoice cleared 🤑,” “payday lands tomorrow 🤑,” or “that came to $180 🤑.” The last example can be sincere or sarcastic; the emoji itself does not resolve it.

It sits differently from 💸, which reports money already spent, and from 💰, which can simply mean money or wealth. 🤑 tends to dramatize wanting cash. A sincere payday message, a self-aware joke about a side hustle, and a smug celebration of getting paid can all use it. The same face can flatter the sender’s earnings or insult the other person’s budget, especially when attached to a price. Read the sentence around it, not just the grin.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🤑 usually appears after the good or painful part of a money update: a payment arrives, payday is close, a side hustle starts paying off, or a quote feels absurd. “invoice cleared 🤑” says the sender is pleased. “me finally explaining this side hustle 🤑” turns income into a self-aware joke. It can also follow a purchase or price when the sender wants to make the amount itself the punchline.

The strongest use is sentence-ending. It frames the line as anticipation, smugness, or disbelief rather than adding detailed financial information. When the amount matters, the emoji cannot supply it, so pair it with a figure or a date if someone needs to know what they owe, when money is coming, or how serious the offer is.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
The clearest problem is price context. “that came to $180 🤑” may mean “I cannot believe I am paying this much” or “I cannot believe you are charging me this much.” One reader sees greed; another sees the sender as broke. Ask for the amount plainly, or use 💸 when money has already been spent.

Also skip 🤑 in serious money discussions where you need one unambiguous meaning. A client message about overdue payment, a family budget talk, or a request for reimbursement can turn the joke into arrogance or an accusation. Name the number and date, or use 💰✨ when the point is simply that money is ready to spend. If you are joking about your own income, make that clear rather than relying on the face to soften it.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone celebrates incoming money with 🤑, you can match the joke with 💵 for cash arriving or 💰✨ for “go spend it.” If they make a smug remark about being paid, laugh along only if the tone supports it; a question such as “how much?” keeps the conversation moving without endorsing the flex. For a vague repayment joke, respond with a clear number and date and 💸.

When 🤑 follows your own price, the face may sting because it can sound like greed or mockery. If the amount is real, restate it directly and offer a specific payment date. If it was only a joke, ask “too much?” rather than guessing. When 🤑 appears under someone else’s price, the cheapest clarification is “what did you think I was charging?”

faqs.question: What does 🤑 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: It usually means he is excited about money, showing off his income, or joking about a price. The sentence matters more than the sender’s gender.

faqs.question: Is 🤑 flirty?
faqs.answer: 🤑 is not inherently flirtatious. It can appear in a flirtatious conversation when money is the joke, but the surrounding words determine whether it feels playful, boastful, or insulting.

faqs.question: What does 🤑 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: In a TikTok caption or comment, it can signal anticipation about money, an ironic income flex, or disbelief about a price. Without nearby context, the face remains intentionally ambiguous.

faqs.question: Why does 🤑 mean both rich and broke?
faqs.answer: The same face can celebrate money arriving or complain that a price is too high. Without the surrounding sentence, 🤑 does not distinguish between having money, wanting it, and finding an expense absurd.

conversationExamples.interpretation: This may be a playful complaint about the bill, but it could also sound like a criticism of the other person’s choice. Respond with “worth it though?” before assuming they are complaining about paying.
The sender is celebrating money arriving and probably expects a cheerful reaction. Match it with 💵, congratulate them, or joke about what they will spend next.

This is casual excitement about getting paid, not necessarily a serious financial question. A coworker can respond with “finally” or 💵; a manager should probably avoid matching the joke in a broad channel.
The sender may be astonished by the total, but the emoji can also imply that whoever paid was being extravagant. Ask who covered it and whether they need help splitting it.

conversationExamples.message: the payment cleared, and suddenly i’m a finance expert 🤑
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a self-aware boast about receiving money. The joke should stay focused on the sender; replying with 💵 keeps it playful, while asking “how much?” continues the financial joke.
